newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE PM PERSUADES TOP MAS OFFICIAL TO STAY.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE PM PERSUADES TOP MAS OFFICIAL TO STAY.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong has persuaded a key Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) official not to resign, a statement from the Prime Minister's office said on Friday.
It said Goh had met MAS deputy managing director Koh Beng Seng and persuaded him to shelve his resignation.
"Mr Koh Beng Seng has played a major role in regulating, supervising and developing Singapore's financial services sector to its present levels," it said.
The statement said Goh had assured Koh he still had much to contribute to the de facto central bank.
It said Koh would help in a government review of measures to promote and further develop Singapore's fast growing financial services sector.
An MAS spokesman told Reuters on August 2 that Koh had tendered his resignation the previous week but that it had not been accepted.
Local newspapers have reported that Koh was set on leaving the MAS and would be gone before the end of the year.
